title: Shiva Temples in Vietnam: What My Son's Records Say

beats.say: Vietnam's My Son has Shiva temples, about fifteen hundred kilometres from India.
beats.caption: My Son, central Vietnam · ~1,500 km from India's Andamans (straight line)

beats.say: UNESCO dates their culture from the fourth to the thirteenth century.
beats.caption: Cham temple culture: 4th–13th century CE (UNESCO)

beats.say: Among its oldest inscriptions, a king founds a temple to Shiva.
beats.caption: Among the oldest known (Finot 1904; Majumdar 1927): King Bhadravarman's temple

beats.say: That temple, probably wooden, burned. A later king rebuilt it.
beats.caption: Probably wooden (Finot) · burned · rebuilt by King Cambhuvarman

beats.say: He renamed the god. Majumdar read such names as taken from kings.
beats.caption: New name: Cambhubhadresvara · 'named from kings' is Majumdar's reading

beats.say: When Shiva worship arrived is not known, says ICOMOS.
beats.caption: “the exact date is not known” (ICOMOS)

beats.say: ICOMOS recommended 'introduction'. UNESCO's committee wrote: an indigenous society adapting.
beats.caption: ICOMOS: “introduction” · UNESCO Committee, 1999: “an indigenous society adapting”

beats.say: And India's archaeologists have restored three groups of these Shiva temples.
beats.caption: India's ASI restored groups A, H, K · 2017–2022 (Govt of India; My Son board)
